cells.tense: You're here at the desk, and the feeling and the practice are running together.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you already repeat, say out loud what it's taught you — even badly — and stop before you add the next part.
cells.core:
The thing your practice is carrying is shared meaning — you show up for something and it moves you, and you let it keep moving you. That's rare. Most people practicing something either go cold and correct or stay warm and scattered. You're neither. People feel it when you hand something over, because you mean it.

What this balance is free to feed is care about the accuracy of it. You already tell the truth about what you're doing; what's open is telling it more carefully, checking your own reading against the thing itself. Building something worth passing on is mostly that second look. Integration means holding the feeling and the method at once, and you can. Nothing's broken; there's just more room in the same picture.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling and the practice are running together. That's the gift.
cells.verb: charging toward what connects, by feeling
cells.place: a small lamp of repetition, kept lit by attention

cells.tense: You're already ahead of the thing, bracing for the version where they finally understand.
cells.ask: Write out the one structure you think should exist, and don't tell a single person it's finished — keep it unpublished for a week.
cells.core:
Your love for the connection that comes after the conversation is running ahead of the conversation. You can feel the room where the meaning has landed, so you press toward it — and the pressing comes out as teaching, correcting, arranging how it should go. A practice is supposed to be small and quiet. Instead it has become a campaign to get the people around you to feel what you feel by Friday.

The pressure you're holding is what you'd call care. It reads as pace, and pace is why the thing isn't landing: meaning won't arrive on a schedule. Force it and you get agreement, and lose the room it was for. Keep your hand on the practice and off the outcome. Meaning that was going to come will come when the ground is ready for it — not when you've arranged it.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing the meaning past where it can land.

cells.tense: There's a door back there you're still standing at, and it's already behind you.
cells.ask: Take one idea you understand and explain it to someone in two sentences — no self-deprecating opener, no asking permission first.
cells.core:
The practice went quiet. Whether the feeling stopped or the showing-it stopped, something in the middle got left in a room you still live in, and the discipline that was supposed to carry the meaning forward isn't doing anything now. It isn't that there's nothing there — it's that what's there isn't moving outward anymore, so it isn't doing its work either.

What's still available is understanding, the kind that can see how things fit, and that's yours to spend. Energy runs along that line before it comes back into the practice. Put it into one concrete act of thinking out loud for someone and the current has somewhere to return to. You don't need to be more warm first. Start with one small use of what's already in your hands.
cells.sheetLine: The understanding's still there. The using-it went quiet.

cells.tense: You're already passing something on, and you keep calling it just how things are.
cells.ask: Say once, plainly, that a thing you've set up or repeated is yours — no explanation, no apology, just that.
cells.core:
This is doing real work whether or not it's claimed — repetition that has become how people around you know the thing, small lit practice no one is naming as practice. It's shaping what gets shared, and it's shaping it well. It just stays filed under objective reality, or luck, or how things are there.

The cost is that care without a claim gets thin. What a person can't be proud of, they eventually can't defend, and what they can't defend they drift from. You don't have to be more confident than you are. Say this one is mine, in your own plain voice, and let it stand without qualifying it. That's not bragging. It's keeping the lamp lit by admitting you lit it.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping what people share. You just call it how things are.
